marco-customer: Hey team — downloaded api-keys.csv from the console and wired the key into our CI as REPO_API_KEY, but all requests return 401 invalid_api_key. Local curl against the same key on my laptop works. Any ideas?

jamie-support: Sorry you're hitting this, marco. Can you paste the exact curl that worked locally and the failing CI call (sanitized key ok)? Also which shell/container the CI runs in.

marco-customer: curl that works locally:
```
curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Api-Key rk_live_ABC123...xyz' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models
```
CI step (using same env var) shows 401 when we call node script: `node ./scripts/prompt.js` — we log the header in the app and see: `Authorization: Api-Key "rk_live_ABC123...xyz"` (note the extra quotes).

nina-engineer: Ah that log gives it away — the key contains literal double quotes in the env value. How did you populate REPO_API_KEY in CI?

marco-customer: We downloaded the csv, opened in Excel to share with team, copied the cell and pasted into GitLab CI variable input. Thought it was clean.

sam-devops: Excel sometimes keeps the CSV cell quoted. If you copy from the CSV viewer it can include the surrounding quotes. If you paste that into GitLab variables, the quotes become part of the value.

jamie-support: Can you confirm by echoing the env in CI (sanitized)? e.g. `echo "$REPO_API_KEY" | hexdump -C` or `printf '%s' "$REPO_API_KEY" | sed -n 'l'` to show hidden chars/quotes.

marco-customer: Ran `printf '%s' "$REPO_API_KEY" | sed -n 'l'` in CI job and it printed: `"rk_live_ABC123...xyz"` (quotes are part of the value).

nina-engineer: Yep that's the issue — server sees the whole string including quotes, which doesn't match any key, so 401 invalid_api_key. Quick fixes: remove the quotes before saving variable, or run a small transform in CI: `REPO_API_KEY=$(echo "$REPO_API_KEY" | sed 's/^\"//;s/\"$//')` before using it.

sam-devops: Alternative robust step: when importing keys from CSV, use a CSV-aware tool to extract the field (avoids accidental quotes). e.g. `csvcut -c api_key api-keys.csv | sed -n '2p'` or `awk -F\",\" 'NR==2{gsub(/\"/,\"\",$2); print $2}' api-keys.csv` (adjust for your format).

marco-customer: Removing quotes in CI fixed it — requests now succeed. Thanks!

lina-product: Thanks for the report, marco. We should add a short note in the dashboard export docs: "Copying keys from CSV in spreadsheet apps may include extra quotes; use the download file or dashboard copy button." Filing follow-up.

jamie-support: Filed product ticket REDW-1248 to add a tooltip and a small validation step on import. Marking this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Incident-assist: No broader incidents reported for invalid_api_key. Scope: single customer mis-import.

marco-customer: Appreciated — leaving this here in case others run into it.
